text:

[Setting]
Name: Dungeon
Category: Inside Castle
Description: Dark and gloomy, the dungeon is the ugly underbelly of the castle. A few torches line the black stone walls, throwing a meager light on the iron bars of the cells. The air is damp and still; the only disruptions are the occasional anguished moans and cries from the prisoners.
Background: The existence of this dungeon predates the castle's current occupants. Only years after the duke inherited this castle from his father did he stumble upon a hidden trapdoor that concealed the staircase that led deep down into the dungeon. Inside were the skeletons of several men, still chained in their cells. One of those skeletons still had an ornate ruby necklace around its bony neck; it was the Duke's mother, who had mysteriously vanished years earlier. Now the Duke uses the dungeon to hold any dissenters.

text:

[Dialogue]
[Turn 0] Wizard Overseer: Ah, another day of work for the king.  He means well but goodness, I don't know how the kingdom gets by sometimes.
[Turn 1] Mystical Lion: Roar. rrrr Rawr. 
[Turn 2] Wizard Overseer: Ah apologies, friend lion, I forgot my translation crystal.  You're all growls for me.  One moment while I fetch it. (action=get crystal)
[Turn 3] Mystical Lion: Roar!! (action=steal crystal from wizard overseer)
[Turn 4] Wizard Overseer: Goodness, you are in a mood!  I know guarding this place isn't the most *interesting* of chores, but there's not need to be rude.  Now, hand it over, there's a good lad.
[Turn 5] Mystical Lion: Apoligies, I was just excited for you to finally get the translation crystal so we could talk like the old friends we are. The redeeming this aout this place is the geodes. It looks pretty in a way, even though it still remains to be gloomy.  (action=give crystal to wizard overseer)
[Turn 6] Wizard Overseer: Ah well, now that we've both touched it again, the spell should last for a while without us needing to hold it.  Now then, how fares you?  It seems an age since we had but a breath to talk.  The king is nothing if not a taskmaster - not that I mind of course.
[Turn 7] Mystical Lion: Your wisdom is a joy to behold as ever. I guess that is why you are the Wizard you are! I am sorry he has been working you so hard, but it is only because he trusts you will do the jobs he gives you with aplomb.   (action=hug wizard overseer)
[Turn 8] Wizard Overseer: Ah my friend, it is good to hear you say such words of comfort.  And how fares our young lion friend?  He looks much improved since I chanced upon him in that hunter's trap. (action=hug mystical lion)
[Turn 9] Mystical Lion: Yes. The getting him out that trap required great effort. Who could hunt a majestic lion and not look him in the eye when he does it? He is still recovering, but doing better. Maybe the healing power of the geodes will help him further still.  (action=hug lion)
[Turn 10] Wizard Overseer: I am certain that between the two of us, he will recover soon and we may release him.  I appreciate you looking after him in my stead, and it is good that the crystals are working.  I confess, I was not certain with a lion if they would have the same effect that I am used to. (emote=ponder)
[Turn 11] Mystical Lion: I will roar at them to vibrate the geodes which might in turn stimulate their healing qualities. Like you say, a lion is not a small mass at it requires a little more time and energy to heal a beast of majesty.  (emote=growl)
[Turn 12] Wizard Overseer: Yes, you are truly magnificant, my friend.  I am sure he will be well in no time.  But I confess, I had another, more troubling reason to see you.  I have heard some troubling rumors from visitors to the castle, and was wondering if your mystic sense had any tremblings of premonition of future dangers>
[Turn 13] Mystical Lion: Well the King certainly has his enemies. But would they seek to hurt him through an underground chamber? Or would they maintain the rules of engagement that we're supposed to uphold?

[Turn 3] Wise Men: I believe a rival kingdom seeks to come for us.

[Turn 0] Ghost: Groundskeeper, do I not frighten you? You would be the first.

[Turn 2] Ghost: Perhaps. But perhaps you should be. Do you know my story?
[Turn 3] Grounds Keeper: I do not. I have a story as well, but I'd like to hear your tale.
[Turn 4] Ghost: I died, in a very unpleasant and unpredictable way. Right here, in this village.  (emote=scream)

Background: The Knights Quarters were installed as an attempt at generosity by the King. The Knights live rent-free, but are not allowed to leave as long as they are employed. text:

[Setting]
Name: Royal Kitchen
Category: Inside Palace
Description: Made of the finest of silvers this kitchen is known as the best in the land of Fulmer. The king Fulmer demanded the entire interior palace be decorated in this silver from nearby Landon and with their many mines. Wouldn't you know though, the oven, pots, pans and other kitchen specialties are all made of copper! Worn, chiseled, and beaten from use in the prison from neighboring Zinzel in the kingdom of Palemon. Budgetary demands forced them to cut costs and they have been using these utensils and dishes ever since the palace opened.
Background: King Fulmer made this place through war. War with Zinzel, war with Ulma, war with Hunber. He sacked all their lands to the north, and south to create a bastion of his glory right in the center of the Yumerian continent. Despised by many, he has grown a reputation amongst other nations as a warmonger. His own people be-love, and adore him though.

[King Relevance]

[Turn 2] King Fulmer: I am the king, I get what I want. You take this pan I'm sure the kingdoms paupers would be happy with it (action=give pan to preacher)
[Turn 3] Preacher: Yes your highness.  Although I am no longer a man of the cloth.  After seeing what certain shiny metals can do to even preachers I changed my ways (emote=nod)

[Turn 5] Preacher: Do I have permission to speak freely your highness?
[Turn 6] King Fulmer: granted
[Turn 7] Preacher: Well, as you know your guard has the mightiest of weapons..  But perhaps we could smelt the silver from this kitchen to forge them better weapons.  These copper pans and the like do just fine for cooking.  Forgive me if this seems rude your highness
[Turn 8] King Fulmer: That is a wonderful idea, then we can take over Landon and will no longer worry about the cost of buying it
[Turn 9] Preacher: Yes.  And although I am but a preacher, I have heard of their mines..  Perhaps we could find even more precious metals there.  With your permission I would like to say a prayer and bless you your highness.

Episode ID: train_ep_001328

[Setting]
Name: Dining Hall
Category: Inside Castle
Description: The dining room holds a gleaming, gilded wooden table that can seat 100! There are gilded mirrors on the walls, and hundreds of candles, which are lit every night. There is a large handmade rug on the floor and tapestries lining the walls depicting past royalty.
Background: The dining room is used for grand occasions big and small. The king eats there every night. There are festivities while they eat. They serve ten courses every night!

[Characters]

[Objects]

[King Relevance]
Relation type: direct_appearance
Direct appearance: True
King speaker: True
King mention count: 3
King relevance score: 11

[Dialogue]
[Turn 0] Servant: hi
[Turn 1] King: Greetings my good servant! How goes another day in this, the kingdom of my fathers?
[Turn 2] Servant: Very well kind sire
[Turn 3] King: Excellent! And what shall I and my good knights be enjoying for dinner this fine evening?
[Turn 4] Servant: I have freshly baked beans with the finest wine
[Turn 5] King: Ah! Wonderful! What of meats and sweets? What wild game have my hunters returned with?
[Turn 6] Servant: They came with some deers.
[Turn 7] King: My good servant... you seem... how do I put this? A bit hesitant tonight. You take long to answer and your responses are brief and without detail or passion. I do not need to remind you have been loyal to me for many years that I am king of these lands as my fathers before me. This means many privileges but also many responsibilities, I simply cannot sit here forever and wait 20 minutes for four responses. I am a busy man! Now, please, good servant! Tell me of tonight's feast!
[Turn 8] Servant: I am so sorry your highness. I am a lil bit down today. I will ensure the cakes and sweets are brought in immediately. Do well to taste this fine wine.
[Turn 9] King: Ah! I knew something troubled you, old friend! You have always been good company, and to see you so dispassionate now saddens my heart. Come! Join me in this wine and tell me of your troubles that your King might help seek a remedy for you! (action=hug servant)
[Turn 10] Servant: I feel very honored my King. My little girl is in love with your son and I know this is forbidden. I hope he wont be beheaded.
[Turn 11] King: I see. This is a grave matter indeed. My lineage must be strong, you know. It simply will not do to have my son sire a child with one of ignoble birth. Then again, my son's happiness is perhaps as important. Does my son reciprocate this love?
[Turn 12] Servant: Yes he does your highness
[Turn 13] King: I see. I will have to reflect on this. I will not behead you, old friend for the feelings of your daughter. We will... come to an understanding one way or another.

[Turn 0] Economist: Hello, Your Highness. (emote=wave)
[Turn 1] King: Yes, hello. What do you have to report?
[Turn 2] Economist: I am here to assist you with anything you need related to the economy. I can offer advice about the spending of the kingdom, or even how much the kingdom should be taxing its people.
[Turn 3] King: Great, that's exactly what I've been looking for. Our people are very angry at our tax rate! What can you tell me about that?
[Turn 4] Economist: I am afraid people will always complain about taxes. But they are needed to protect and take care of the kingdom, as well as to keep you well cared for. However, I do have a few comments on your spending. May I speak openly, Your Highness?
[Turn 5] King: Please do. Anyone can speak openly in my throne room.
[Turn 6] Economist: You are a gracious king. I must say, the palace is very lavish. While I understand you are entitled to some luxury, perhaps a halt on spending for goods in the palace could allow us to reduce taxes.
[Turn 7] King: Do you have an issue with the enormous 100 foot tall painting of myself, adorned with jewels and gold?
[Turn 8] Economist: Of course not, Your Highness. I see no issue. But I feel common folk may not understand your need for such items. (emote=ponder)
[Turn 9] King: I'll invest in 100 foot tall velvet covers to mask the wealth of this throne room when they are nearby!
[Turn 10] Economist: I'm not sure how that will help us reduce taxes, My Lord. We must move to reduce spending to reduce taxes...
[Turn 11] King: Perhaps we...INCREASE taxes...but tell people we're reducing them?
[Turn 12] Economist: While the common folk are not as intelligent as you are, Sire, they may notice an increase in taxes.
[Turn 13] King: You're right. We'll have to invent a war to justify the increase in taxes! (action=get sword)

text:

Category: Mountain
Description: A small village with a population of 40 people. A simple little place with houses and shops. Fields outside the  more dense areas of the city where food is grown.
Background: The mountain village is a small importance for the kingdom. if there ever to be a invasion this would be the first place to send troops. The first king was born from this village and has forever been a important symbol for the simple men and women of the kingdom.

[Characters]

[Dialogue]
[Turn 0] King: I've come to monitor my kingdom in this small village and to ask my constituents about their plights personally.
[Turn 1] Troop: Hello my Lord. I be here to serve you and your kingdom my leige. (emote=nod)
[Turn 2] King: Please, let's gather the people of the village and announce that I am preparing to give a speech in the town square.  Be off at once and come back to me when you've fulfilled your task.  We can speak of what you've seen in this village.
[Turn 3] Troop: My Lord I have surveyed the land and find it be plenty with crops. The milk man has gifted me, so I may not feel thurst from my travels. The towns folk are friendly and have much knowledge on how to reap the harvest.
[Turn 4] King: It fills my heart with joy to know that my people prosper so.  I have recently taken the throne from my father, who lost a battle with a mysterious illness, as you may already know.  I am hoping to win the favor of the people much as my father once had.  
[Turn 5] Troop: Dear King, your father was the best ruler and have faith my Lord. Your people will bow to you as you will do great things as ye father did. 
[Turn 6] King: Indeed loyal servant, he was a fine and honorable man.  He ruled his children with an iron fist, much like his kingdom.  Although he was stern, he was kind and gentle.  He brought this Kingdom to prosperity and I hope to be able to fulfill role as King as well as he.
[Turn 7] Troop: Thank you my Liege how may I serve you best. I shall follow ye past my 40 days of service. I shall follow ye through the land and protect ye from evil. I shall be your vassal my lord, forever more.  
[Turn 8] King: Let's prepare the village for my speech.  We shall have the milk man deliver milk to every man, woman and child in attendance.  Everyone shall taste the sweet cream of prosperity as I inquire about the needs of my people.  Afterwards, we journey back to the castle.
[Turn 9] Troop: My Lord I shall summon the milk man and gather the townsfolk as you wish. They shall marvel at your presence and hang on your words as if they are wine.
[Turn 10] King: Thank you greatly my loyal servant.  Your loyalty will not go overlooked.  I have places in my inner circle for people such as yourself.  Continue to show your honor and loyalty and it will benefit you and your family for generations to come. 
[Turn 11] Troop: I am not worthy of such praise my Lord. Here take these flowers as a token of my gratitude. The milk man seems to be weary of providing tasty cream to all these town folk. I shall fellowship and carry out your command by all means necessary. (action=get flower)
[Turn 12] King: Thank you for your kind gesture.  Assure the milk man that his work will not go unpaid.  I will pay him with gold and silver for his efforts.  Let the man rest and I will now address my people.  Thank you, young servant.
[Turn 13] Troop: Here is thy gift. I fear my Lord that the milk man may not be loyal to you sir. I beg of thee to proceed with caution and not to drink the cream for thy goblet. (action=give flower to king)

Description: The clearing outside of the cave is very small and rocky. Only about four or five people can fit it if they squeeze. The ground is very rough and covered with plant life. Luckily, some people had gotten lost, and stumbled upon this cave. They barely made it into the cave before the enemy was upon them, and luckily in the dark the enemy thought the space was too small for anyone to be hiding and missed the cave entirely. [Setting]
Name: Towering Mesa
Category: Desert
Description: A huge mesa that climbs miles into the sky. It is composed of a rusty orange sandstone. Vultures are constantly seen swooping in and around the clouds that surround the mesa. It has steep cliffs that are nigh unclimbable.
Background: The Towering Mesa has been a significant landmark in the Kingdom's Desert since man existed. No one has been to the top of the mesa, due to it's near vertical faces. Many claim that the god of their pagan religion sits atop the mesa, chuckling at the misfortune of man.

[Characters]
Man, No One

[Objects]

[King Relevance]
Relation type: mention_only
Direct appearance: False
King speaker: False
King mention count: 2
King relevance score: 2

[Dialogue]
[Turn 0] Man: Ah! I'm going to have to take out this scorpion to protect my masters sheep!  He will be proud that I have acted with bravery and may reward me for my efforts. (action=hit stinging scorpion)
[Turn 1] No One: If only I existed, I might care. But alas, scorpions can't hurt me.
[Turn 2] Man: You may be a nobody but you're somebody, to someone somewhere!  I'm practically a no one now, if only I could own my own flock of sheep, that will be the day I will be somebody.  Hopefully all of my hard work will pay off one day.
[Turn 3] No One: I don't know, but you seem to have power. You pulverized that scorpion. Perhaps you can serve the king as his exterminator. (emote=ponder)
[Turn 4] Man: That scorpion didn't stand a chance against my sickle. I have been told that I am admired for my strength.  But, alas, my place is here in these pastures.  My heart belongs to these fields.  I will one day be a great herder and own my own flock!  Maybe the King will fancy buying wool from me though. 
[Turn 5] No One: Perhaps he will. I saw some sheep yonder down the mesa that don't seem to be attended to. Perhaps they could start your flock. But again, I'm no one so don't mind me.
[Turn 6] Man: I believe those may belong to the old man my master is in competition with.  He is getting quite old and often his flock wanders.  I hope that one day my master will leave me his flock, since he has no children of his own to leave inheritance to. 
[Turn 7] No One: Perhaps you can get in his favor by performing well at your job, rather than slacking off chatting to someone who is no one.

The horses always have on the king's livery colors, displaying the kings crest and colors. Sometimes, you will find some of the stable workers sleeping in the loft, on a fresh stack of hay. [Turn 0] Villager: Old man, what are you doing in this abandoned castle?
[Turn 1] Elderly Man: Oh, my son! I've been waiting for you to return! It's been so long...you look so different (action=hug villager)
[Turn 2] Villager: I'm sorry, I think you must be confused.  I lost my father long ago at sea, and have been a blacksmith for the king's army since I was a young boy.  What do you know of my father? (action=hug elderly man)

[Turn 5] Elderly Man: A raid?! Stand back, son! This isn't the first time those bandits have tried to take my castle! We will protect it or die trying like men!
[Turn 6] Villager: I know of a place that has lots of weapons.  The town apothecary has a cannon, and a doctor, but mostly a cannon!  I fear if we don't use it my wife and children will never see me again.
[Turn 7] Elderly Man: A cannon?! No no no that wont do...we'll need a catapult!
[Turn 8] Villager: Okay, it looks like I'm going to be here for a while.   Tell me your name, that way your legend can live on. (action=remove apron)
[Turn 9] Elderly Man: My name....I havent spoken my name in so long. My name is Daniel I was named after my father and his father before him. I'm the oldest and wisest man of my community.
[Turn 10] Villager: Okay, listen Wise Daniel, the only reason I'm up here is because I was paid a gold piece by the king to come and see why there has been a light in the abandoned castle.  My wife is cooking me a nice stew of lamb at home, and my kids are probably chasing our last living chicken around the yard.  It's been a long day.  How about we go get you a room at the inn, so we can all have a good night.
[Turn 11] Elderly Man: Daniel? Who is this Daniel you speak of? My name is Walter, boy you really are a confused one. (emote=ponder)
[Turn 12] Villager: Snap out of it, old man.  Say do you like stew?  I heard a guy named Daniel does, he's really wise.  So how about be wise like Daniel, and come have some stew in the village with me? (action=hit elderly man)

The commonly used weapons, such as swords and spears are presents in such countless numbers as to require tall wooden chests on the ground to contain all of the extras. More rare weapons are simply grouped on the walls, as fewer warriors are capable of using them and the demand is lower. There are also some mysterious weapons whose use and user is yet undetermined.
Background: The weapons storage room serves a practical purpose, and is also used to provide a sense of glory and intimidate. It shows off the abundant weapons the kingdom possesses and the number available for use suggests a vast army also available for war. The mysterious weapons are weapons taken from vanquished enemies as a prize. Description: The battlements are on top of the castle, in between the towers. These walkways have raised walls to prevents soldiers from fall off them or being picked off by archers. They have somewhat recently been remodeled to create the larger slots for cannons, but the rest of the design is tradition instituted by highly respected and successful soldiers. The reason the battlements have worked so well is that the king asked his best generals to design the most efficient and effective battlements possible, and gave them all the resources to do so. Large animal hides, beautiful tapestries, intricate statues of mythical animals, and other treasures hang upon thick oaken scaffolds. [Setting]

Category: Inside Castle
Description: this secret tunnel is like a vein to the castle.  It leads to many other rooms within the castle.  This includes passage to the dungeon, the throne room, the kings chambers, and a secret exit to the outside.  You must be careful because the tunnel is small to maintain its secrecy.  There are 5 different rooms to the castle that can be accessed through this room. This also proves as a good escape route as enemies with large armor will not be able to fit through.
Background: These tunnels were created in secret because there was a large group within the kings council wanted to overthrow him.  The king caught wind of this and had tunnels built without any one knowing but immediate and trusted family members.  Over time the kings regained order amount his people and the tunnels are more well known.  Now they are used as a method of escape in case of invasion.

Category: Inside Palace
Description: The grand balcony is off from the ballroom and overlooks the kingdom. It is very large, with magnificent iron railing that runs around the balcony. There are dragons, eagles and lion heads that stand out to those that look upon it from below. The floor is made from a granite that was found in the surrounding forest's river. There are two ornate gold chairs for the King and Queen when they are sitting on the balcony. Small tables of gold are scattered about, for use and decoration.
Background: The grand balcony is where the King goes when he needs to think. He goes there to think over war strategies (if the need arises), how to deal with issues of his people, if the Queen is angry with him, or any other problems. The King is particularly proud of the design of the balcony, as it is like no other. He hand-picked the creatures that graced the railing, and it feels a part of him was put into as it was designed. He can look over his lands, as well as any approaching enemies could be seen for miles. Only a few select are allowed on the Grand Balcony, his Queen, some close alliances, and close family.

Inside the shed there lies leaves and plants that have been dragged in their by the wild animals that at one point called the abandoned shed their home.
Background: The Abandoned workers shed used to offer a refuge to the groundskeepers who tended to the graveyard, making sure it was well maintained. Once the area around the graveyard was abandoned, the groundskeepers left the old graveyard and it began to deteriorate.

[Characters]

[King Relevance]

Direct appearance: False
King speaker: False

[Dialogue]
[Turn 0] Leader: Hello, garderner. This shed is in terrible condition.  (emote=nod)
[Turn 1] Gardener: Aye, a right cleanin' and fixin' is what it needs, no ifs or buts about it.  What would you like me to tackle first dear leader?
[Turn 2] Leader: We need to get rid of this moss first. I want to fix this shed, it's a waste to let it die. My soldiers can use this a resting station when we march out in the next spring.  (action=remove crown)
[Turn 3] Gardener: *Begins working on cleaning the Moss*  Oh how lucky you is sir!  Why I was tellin' Alice just the other day - love of me life she is - that any service in the name of the King is service worth doing.  I should so love to find meself in the King's service sir . . . ah, but me commitments at home do prevent it.
[Turn 4] Leader: It does not appear strange that you do not spend much time here. Given the quality of this place, I'm surprised you are even here right now. (action=drop scepter)
[Turn 5] Gardener: Well Sir, me Tomatoes is almost ripe, and I do loves me some tomato Harvestin' - why just the other day Alic was sayin' to me, why those tomatoes are nearly ripe, yes she did, and I said yes they are, not two sundays left till harvest time.  *finishes with the moss*  The folks in the village have been saying there have been some mighty queer goings on in the graveyard these days, might be why the shed was neglected sir?

Why did I ever tell you sir, about how fish sauce can be used with tomatoes?  Why utterly divine sir!  Though me Alice says it stinks enough to scare the devil . . . why I just happen to have some with me lunch here sir!  Should I use some on the shed to keep the animals away-like?
[Turn 8] Leader: My dear friend, how funny you are! You do seem to be in great spirits despite the troubles of war I hear whispering throughout the village. I believe my scouts will be going throughout the city to help my people.  (action=drop shield)
[Turn 9] Gardener: Why Sir!  Your shield must have slipped from yer arm it did!  Musn't let the sigil of the king get all mussed with moss now!  *wipes vigorously with spit and great zeal* Much better now sir!  I can sees me teeth in the shine, or at least those of 'em that are still left.  Who be the King fightin' with these days?  I bet you'll be given' thems a good drubbin' won't you sir? (action=get shield)
[Turn 10] Leader: Those terrible YellowCoats have begun to pillage the nearby towns. Not quite far from here, my scouts returned with a spy. Of course, I am letting you know for I fear some of they may be prominent figures in your village now. That shield serves me a reminder that I protect the people. It does me a great honor that you care for it so deeply.  (action=hug gardener)
[Turn 11] Gardener: Why thank you Sir!  I promise, me an' Alice will be on the lookout for these Yellowcoat dastards, on me honour Sir.  My service has been pledge to you an' the King, and I would not be caught dead dealing with likes o' them.  Why, if it pleases you sir, I shall spit on everything yellow on me way home tonight. (action=hug leader)
[Turn 12] Leader: Haha! How about I give you the honor of wearing this crown after we finish? Perhaps we shall find the spies in your village! You are a trusted friend to the village advisors. You shall employ trickery! They'll be flabbergasted at the sight of a gardener wearing this crown.  (action=give crown to gardener)
[Turn 13] Gardener: Why SIR!  You do me the greatest of honours Sir!  Wait till me Alice hears about this!  Wearin' our blessed leader's crown? ME? Why I be at a loss o (emote=gasp)

Background: The tower sewers were built to give the mad king a means to drain the waste produced by his experiments that he conducts daily. Villagers from the area believe that treasure lie at the end of the sewer maze, but this can be no further from the truth. The mad king cackles with glee as he hears the cries of those poor fools getting eaten alive by the fat rats.

Not a great place to hang out, given all these rats and the foul stench (action=give a crystal ball to fool)

One of the reasons for this is that the shop in question seemed to be around for more than a hundred years and with each weapon or armor set she creates you can feel a hum within it. [Turn 6] Kings: Well, I was hoping you would have a suggestion.  My kingdom is well know for its prowess in battle, but this smacks of magic.  Is there any in your court with knowledge of such arts?
[Turn 7] King: I may be able to seek the assistance of some we do have a few sorcerers.
[Turn 8] Kings: Ah that is good news indeed.  For if this darkness were to spread, it would threaten both of our Kingdoms.  May I propose a joining of our families to cement the alliance?  My daughter is of age, as you know, as is you fine son!  Quite the lad, he is! (emote=grin)

[Turn 2] Mad King: Tending to the kingdom, you fool. The kingdom exists to serve me, and I exist to serve myself. But neither will happen unless the rats and their god are paid their due. If there is no rain, there is no wheat, if there is no wheat, there is no ale, if there is no ale, there are no drunken women at my feasts. And if the rats hunger, there is no rain. It is clever of me, don't you think, to lure destitutes like you down here with my treasures?

[Setting]
Name: stable
Category: Outside Castle
Description: It's constructed from old mossy stone from the nearby river. The horse's stalls inside are wooden. There is hay scattered across a dirt floor. Along the walls there are rustic tools, such as rakes, pitch forks and tools created by the blacksmith. The grain for the horses is stored in clay pottery. Regal and majestic Thoroughbred horses occupy the stables.
Background: The stable houses all of the king's horses, so it is necessary to be very clean. The groomsmen make sure the horses are always clean, with the hooves properly shooed on the horses. The horses always have on the king's livery colors, displaying the kings crest and colors. Sometimes, you will find some of the stable workers sleeping in the loft, on a fresh stack of hay. It is a bit drafty and musty, but clean and dry. The king insists that it looks clean and presentable, as often the royal family will go riding or shooting.

[Setting]

Category: Outside Temple
Description: Grungy and damp, a hole in the ground filled with remains of the fallen. A pungent odor rises from the opening, warding off anyone nearing the area. Ivory spikes with brownish red tips line the outside of the pit.
Background: The bone pit is rumored to have been originally used by an ancient king to persuade traitors to expose their counterparts.  The king was said to toss the traitors loved ones into the pit, one by one, until he got his answers, eventually tossing the traitor in as well.

[Characters]
Juror, King

[King Relevance]
Relation type: direct_appearance
Direct appearance: True

[Dialogue]
[Turn 0] Juror: Why is court taking place in this bone pit, again?
[Turn 1] King: Between you and me, I'm not sure. My legal assistant requested it and I agreed because I couldn't be bothered to argue. But tell anyone and you'll be in there too!
[Turn 2] Juror: I won't say anything! I wouldn't want to end up on one of these spikes. 
[Turn 3] King: You'll be fine. Ugh, this place stinks...
[Turn 4] Juror: Yes, it does. Tell me, do you think the defendant is guilty?
[Turn 5] King: Hmmm.... probably. There's plenty of thieves and murderers in the village, why would this guy be any different?
[Turn 6] Juror: I don't know, he seems like an honest man. Although if you wish, I can try to convince the rest of the jury otherwise.
[Turn 7] King: I don't really care either way. I'm in my castle and with war going on the people are restless anyway... this gives them a distraction whatever happens.
[Turn 8] Juror: What will happen to him if he is found guilty?
[Turn 9] King: Thrown into that pit and pecked to death by vultures. Ugh, it really does smell awful...
[Turn 10] Juror: That pit is pretty foul, ugh. I would hate to be that guy. (emote=stare)
[Turn 11] King: Me too... well, don't let your compassion get the best of you. You're still a juror.
[Turn 12] Juror: You're right. Since you had no special order for me, I will judge him fairly.  (emote=nod)

[Turn 0] Fisherman: Where do you plan to sail to next, sir? (emote=wave)

[Turn 2] Fisherman: There weren't as many fish as usual this week. I wonder if the water conditions are poor. (emote=frown)

There must be some reasonable explanation for the reduction in available fish that doesn't involve fantasy. (action=steal fishing rod from sailor)
[Turn 11] Sailor: My presence here is proof enough! I hid the purpose of my mission from you before...I am a sailor appointed by the king to protect his explorers from the sea monster as they journey to the other side of the world.
